Commentary.Commentary: We are back. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis have walked out as the openers for Sri Lanka with Richard Ngarava ready to bowl the first over of the chase.
... The Run Chase ...

With Sri Lanka needing 192 runs to win, Zimbabwe appears to have the upper hand at the halfway stage, given Sri Lanka's recent batting struggles. However, Sri Lanka is a quality side, and their ability to bounce back shouldn't be underestimated. The stage is set for an exciting chase, and it's anyone's game.

Tadiwanashe Marumani, the half-centurion for Zimbabwe, is up for a chat. He says that they had a blueprint for every phase, but he just gave himself a bit of time. Adds that it was more about trusting himself out there and reckons it is a par score as the wicket looks good. Ends by saying that he hopes the bowlers can defend it.

Sri Lanka's bowling performance was subpar, with runs leaking throughout the park and a significant number of extras conceded. Dushan Hemantha was the standout wicket-taker with 3 wickets, while Dushmantha Chameera took 2 wickets. Charith Asalanka bowled economically but failed to pick up any wickets. Binura Fernando and Matheesha Pathirana also chipped in with a wicket each.

The top 3 batters for Zimbabwe showcased their intent with an aggressive approach, forging crucial partnerships. The first wicket partnership added 26 runs off 15 balls, followed by 39 runs off 26 balls for the second wicket, and a 56-run partnership off 36 balls for the third wicket. This solid foundation helped Zimbabwe post a substantial total. Notably, every batter got a start, and Tadiwanashe Marumani stood out by converting his start into a half-century, ultimately top-scoring for the hosts.

At the halfway stage of the match, Zimbabwe, having batted first, would be delighted to have posted a total of 191 runs. Their problem throughout this tour has been not finishing well with the bat, but that was not the case here. Despite losing wickets, the intent was there from every batter, and that is why they have posted such a big total.

FOUR! A boundary to end the inning! Much fuller on off and middle. Richard Ngarava drills hard toward the right of the wide long on fielder and gets four more runs added to the total. Zimbabwe finish on 191/8!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start the inning! The umpires have stepped on the field and so are the players of Sri Lanka. Brian Bennett will be opening with Tadiwanashe Marumani for Zimbabwe. Matheesha Pathirana will get the job to start with the new ball. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo is pitchside. He says he got the first innings total very wrong in the last game. Russell Arnold joins him and says that there are a lot of cracks and they are wide open on one side. Mentions that there will be uneven bounce and the batters will need to assess the conditions, but it won't be easy. They walk up to the other side and Russell points out that the cracks there are not that wide and they are more subcontinental-like. Tino says it is not a 180 pitch, more like a 140.

Justin Sammons, the Head Coach of Zimbabwe, is up for a quick chat. He says they put Sri Lanka under pressure with early wickets, but the great thing was they kept it on throughout. Adds that they did lose a few wickets as well, but kept their composure to chase down the target. Mentions that as a coach, it is always important to keep the spirits high in the camp. Says that the players have performed well, and they understand the process and journey. Further adds that it is brilliant to play a series decider like this before the qualifiers, as there will be pressure on them there, but if they manage to win this, they will go with a lot of confidence and momentum.

Zimbabwe (Unchanged Playing XI) - Brian Bennett, Tadiwanashe Marumani (WK), Sean Williams, Sikandar Raza (C), Ryan Burl, Tony Munyonga, Tashinga Musekiwa, Brad Evans, Tinotenda Maposa, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kamil Mishara, Kusal Perera (In place of Nuwanidu Fernando), Charith Asalanka (C), Kamindu Mendis, Dasun Shanaka, Dushan Hemantha, Matheesha Pathirana (In place of Maheesh Theekshana), Dushmantha Chameera, Binura Fernando.

Sikandar Raza, skipper of Zimbabwe, says that he would have bowled first as well. Adds that in the first game, they scored a lot of runs, and Raza believes that they can pull out the same performance. Continues that they have got a lot of variations in terms of bowlers, and he will look forward to utilize it in this match. Also says that he got hit around his ribs, there's a bit niggle, but a lot better now. Ends up saying that it is a good opportunity for them to go forward as a team. Informs that they are unchanged.

Sri Lanka captain Charith Asalanka emphasized the importance of utilizing the larger boundary wisely. Asalanka also outlined the batting approach, advising his players to hit gaps and run hard, targeting the opposite side of the field. Despite the significant defeat in the previous match, Asalanka believes it's essential to bounce back fresh and use the pressure as a catalyst for improvement in T20 cricket. Informs they have made a couple of changes in the team.
TOSS - Charith Asalanka calls 'HEADS,' and he is correct. Sri Lanka have elected to BOWL first.

Sri Lanka's batting performance in the second T20I was nothing short of disastrous. The team was bundled out for just 80 runs, with only Kamil Mishara showing some resistance with a run-a-ball 20. The rest of the batting lineup struggled to cope with the Zimbabwean bowlers, who were ruthless in their execution. With the series decider looming, Sri Lanka will need to regroup and come up with better plans to take on a determined Zimbabwean side. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

Zimbabwe's momentum is high after their impressive win in the second T20I, where they bowled Sri Lanka out for just 80 runs. Sikandar Raza and Brad Evans excelled, taking three wickets each. Despite a rocky start, Zimbabwe's batters successfully chased down the target, thanks to Ryan Burl and Tashinga Musekiwa's crucial partnership. To seal the series win, Zimbabwe needs to build on their strong bowling performance and focus on improving their batting consistency.

It's time for the thrilling conclusion to the T20I series between Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka! The two teams are set to clash in an intense series decider at the Harare Sports Club. After a closely contested first T20I, where Sri Lanka emerged victorious, Zimbabwe bounced back strongly in the second match to level the series 1-1.
.. MATCHDAY ...

We have arrived at the final game of Sri Lanka’s tour of Zimbabwe, with the final T20I match set to be played between them at Harare Sports Club. The visitors, Sri Lanka, have dominated most of the tour. Still, the hosts, Zimbabwe, made a terrific comeback in the second T20I to level the series 1-1, and we are all set for a thriller decider in the last match of the tour. To begin the T20I series with a victory, the visitors outwitted the hosts. Dushmantha Chameera, who rejoined the team, has been outstanding with the ball in the opening game, taking three wickets to keep the opposition to a manageable total. Every other bowler joined him in contributing. Chameera maintained his explosive form with the ball and helped Zimbabwe make early inroads while defending a modest 80-run total in the previous game as well. The bowlers will be motivated to continue their strong display to win. The Sri Lankan batters need to fix their problems in the batting lineup for this match, as they failed to perform in the second game after chasing down 176 in the first. To win this game and score important runs at the top, their chances will once again depend on their openers, Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis. They will also look to captain Charith Asalanka and batter Kamindu Mendis, who had a strong performance in the first T20I, to provide middle-order consistency and post a big total. After sweeping away the Sri Lankans for their second-lowest total in T20Is, the home squad enters this match with confidence and momentum. On cue, their bowlers drew a comeback in the second T20I and have set up a series decider. In addition to Brad Evans and Blessing Muzarabani's assistance in the bowling department, captain Sikandar Raza has been top-notch in his all-around performance. But as of right now, their batting appears to be a little off course, and the only bright spot in their batting lineup is Brian Bennett. Additionally, in the last match, they collapsed a bit as well while attempting to chase the low total. To contribute in this crunch game and establish some rhythm with the bat, they would need their seasoned campaigners, such as Sean Williams and Ryan Burl, to perform. The game at Harare Sports Club is expected to be an exciting one, with the visitors hoping to win to end the series and get into the Asia Cup with momentum on their side. However, the hosts, Zimbabwe, will hope to turn the T20I series in their favour after losing the ODI series. Who are you rooting for?
